extracted.intended_audience: writers and line editors (fiction and nonfiction) seeking to improve sentence-level craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for line editing prose at the sentence level, focusing on rhythm, cadence, word choice, punctuation, and sound to improve flow, clarity, and impact. Applicable to fiction and literary nonfiction for refining sentence-level texture and avoiding common rhythmic failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Select precise diction so that no easier word would do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line editing polishes word choice; aim for precision and exactness. Avoid generic or vague words; prefer words that carry the exact meaning and tone intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape sentence length and cadence to create flow and momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A line editor reads for flow — mark where prose stumbles, energy flags, or word choice muddles meaning. Use sentence-length variation and punctuation to control pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistent and appropriate tonal register at the sentence level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line editing refines tone so sentence-level choices (word, cadence, punctuation) support overall voice and scene mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey internal thought, feeling, and point of view clearly and vividly in sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sentence-level techniques (fragments, cadence, diction) to render interiority without collapsing into exposition or cliché.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sentence-to-sentence connections are smooth and logical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line editing addresses where prose stumbles by fixing weak or abrupt transitions so ideas and actions flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show vs. tell
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor showing through concrete detail and active phrasing rather than telling in abstract statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the sentence level, convert telling sentences into showing when possible; reduce abstract noun-heavy constructions and prefer sensory, active detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate unnecessary words so sentences are lean and purposeful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove filler and redundant constructions; prefer economical phrasing without losing nuance or necessary rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose words with exact semantic and connotative fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diction precision overlaps with word choice: avoid vague synonyms, pick words that align with character, tone, and scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary Sentence Length
rubrics_metrics.description: The #1 rhythm rule: vary sentence length to avoid monotony and control pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short sentences hit hard; longer, flowing sentences carry the reader forward, accumulating clauses and momentum. Aim for average 10–20 words for 'workhorse' sentences. Consider genre signals: thriller writers tend shorter; literary writers tend longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short, Short, Long (rhythmic pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the pattern of two short sentences followed by a longer one to create reliable rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short sentences deliver impact; the following long sentence carries and resolves momentum. Employ deliberately to vary pace and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence Fragments (purposeful use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use fragments deliberately to create emphasis, speed, intimacy, or interrupted thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragments can heighten immediacy or mimic thought. Warning: used too often they become a tic; use sparingly and with clear intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation as Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commas, semicolons, dashes, ellipses, and periods to shape pacing and rests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat punctuation like musical rests and dynamics—choose marks to slow, speed, interrupt, or extend breath. Be intentional rather than mechanical with punctuation choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound Patterning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use alliteration, internal rhyme, consonance, and assonance deliberately to enhance musicality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sound devices sparingly and purposefully. Be alert for unintentional rhymes or patterns that distract the reader rather than support meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read Aloud Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Read prose aloud to detect stumbles, monotony, or awkward rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it stumbles or feels monotonous when read aloud, revise. The ear is a primary editor of sentence rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match Rhythm to Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Align sentence rhythm with the scene's content: action, reflection, tension, or lyric description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action: short, punchy sentences; Reflection: longer, more complex sentences; Tension: clipped sentences; Lyric description: musical, flowing sentences. Let content dictate cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No two consecutive sentences have the same length/structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid repeating sentence length or structure back-to-back to prevent monotony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary both length and syntactic structure between adjacent sentences so energy and interest are sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active verbs predominate
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor active-voice verbs to increase immediacy and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active constructions over passive ones where appropriate; active verbs help carry momentum and sharpen images.

rubrics_metrics.name: No filler ('there is', 'it is')
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid weak filler constructions such as 'there is' and 'it is'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace filler with stronger, more specific constructions that show rather than pad sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifiers used sparingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit adverbs and stacked modifiers so sentences remain clear and strong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune modifier clusters and prefer vivid nouns and verbs instead of relying on adverbs to do heavy lifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and meaning align
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sonic choices (rhythm, alliteration, assonance) reinforce, not contradict, semantic meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match musical qualities of sentences to their content and tone; avoid pleasing sounds that undermine clarity or seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: The page has a 'texture' you can hear
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective sentence-level craft produces an audible texture or voice across the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a coherent aural texture through consistent but varied rhythms, diction, and sound patterning so the prose reads as a unified voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotony: all sentences average 12 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure mode where sentences all cluster around the same mid-length, producing monotony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid uniform sentence length; introduce short and long sentences to create dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on compound-complex sentences ('sludge')
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure mode of overusing compound-complex constructions that clog prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break up overlong, heavily qualified sentences that slow reading; prioritize clarity and forward motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in long, qualified sentences (energy drain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure mode where action scenes are written in long, qualifying sentences and lose momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shorter, punchier sentences for action to preserve pace and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection in choppy short sentences (no breath)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure mode where reflective passages are rendered in too-short sentences that feel breathless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give reflective passages longer, more complex sentences to allow development and nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive openings ('She walked. She turned. She looked.')
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure mode of repetitive sentence openings that create tedium and blunt characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary sentence openings, verb choice, and structure to avoid mechanical repetition; use varied syntactic constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverb clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure mode of over-relying on multiple adverbs to modify verbs or adjectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune adverb clusters; instead strengthen verbs or choose more precise modifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'To be' verb chains
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure mode of sequences of 'to be' verbs that produce weak, static prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace 'to be' chains with active verbs or reframe sentences to show action and change.
